correctness.rationale: Plancherel reduces the exact operator norm to \(2^k\max_{0\le t\le1}t^{k/2}|1-bt|\). For \(b\le1\) the objective decreases pointwise with \(b\); for \(b>1\) its two branch maxima are exactly \(c_r b^{-r}\) and \(b-1\), so the unique minimizer is their unique crossing. The Fourier-positivity condition is exactly \(b\le1\). The asymptotic follows from the defining equation after setting \(y_r=r(b_r-1)\). The packaged verifier reproduces the branch equalities and known low-order constants.

value.rationale: The support radius is a central parameter of the smoothest-average problem, and n=1 is its first nontrivial case. The theorem gives a natural complete classification at that cutoff for every derivative order, fills exact finite-radius instances of several cells the recent source marks open at general radius, identifies a universal Fourier-positive optimizer, and quantifies the all-order asymptotic gap. This is more than a numerical recomputation or arbitrary parameter slice.
